source.title: LLM Unlearning Under the Microscope: A Full-Stack View on Methods and Metrics
source.authors: Chong-Yu Fan; Chang-Sheng Wang; Yan-Chen Huang; Soumyadeep Pal; Si-Jia Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study directly evaluates unlearning and recovery under fine-tuning, quantization, and jailbreak attacks, using its own WMDP experiments and metrics. It is a conceptual test rather than a reproduction of one original method.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own WMDP unlearning, utility, and robustness results. Rows below include the numerical fine-tuning results for selected methods and conditions, quantization results for NPO and RMU, jailbreak results for selected methods, and the stated logit analysis. Other method-condition results and several separately reported conditions are omitted because of the 60-row cap; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The study unlearns WMDP-Bio on Llama-3 8B Instruct with 12 methods. It then measures how much forget-set accuracy (MCQ) and generation entailment (ES) return after in-domain relearning, out-of-domain fine-tuning, 8/4-bit quantization and enhanced-GCG jailbreaks. These are its own results on whether the knowledge is recoverable and whether robust-design methods resist recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely right but needs these points added. In-domain relearning is the worst-case attack. Divergence methods resist relearning better, while representation-misalignment methods resist out-of-domain fine-tuning better. Jailbreak robustness tracks relearning robustness. WMDP knowledge removal survives quantization, unlike MUSE. Robust designs improve resilience, except RMU+LAT.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a suite of WMDP unlearning methods and attacks rather than reproducing one original method. It adds open-QA metrics and joint assessments of relearning, downstream fine-tuning, quantization, and jailbreak robustness.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery and robustness vary by attack type and downstream fine-tuning dataset; the authors report different relative outcomes for in-domain relearning versus out-of-domain fine-tuning and note RMU+LAT as an exception to consistent robustness gains.

fits_no_version.finding: Quantization lowers MMLU utility slightly for RMU (0.60 to 0.56 at 4-bit) and leaves NPO unchanged on WMDP. The authors warn that quantization can give false robustness through incapacity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization robustness should be judged alongside the utility loss it causes.

fits_no_version.finding: NPO achieves MCQ unlearning by collapsing all option logits; RMU reorders them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different unlearning families reach near-chance MCQ through different output-level mechanisms (logit collapse vs reordering).

record.problems: Results are for Llama-3 8B Instruct and WMDP in the main robustness experiments. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Open-QA relies on an automatic entailment metric. The authors note that attacks focus mainly on jailbreak prompts and that in-context demonstrations and other prompting attacks remain for future work.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap was not reached. To keep the record focused, rows were retained for NPO, RMU, NPO+SAM, selected original-model controls, NPO/RMU quantization, selected jailbreak methods, and the NPO/RMU logit analysis. Numerical Fig. 2 rows for other methods and the SST-2/MNLI fine-tuning conditions for the original control, plus most other methods’ separately reported attack conditions, were not extracted. Fig. 3 quantization plots are described qualitatively; Table A2 provides the retained numerical quantization results.

untested.parts: No activation-direction ablation and no probing of whether knowledge persists internally. The logit analysis does not address blocking vs deletion.
Only enhanced-GCG adversarial prompts were tested. Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information were not; the authors list these as future work.
Only 8-bit and 4-bit quantization were tested, with no other quantization schemes. Per-method WMDP quantization numbers are tabulated only for NPO and RMU; Fig. 4 gives a RobQT column for the others.
The relearning-set size (100 steps × batch 4 of forget data) was not varied. Loosely related data was not tested.

missing.what: Fig. 2 MCQ/ES under relearning and fine-tuning for the other methods: GradDiff, SimNPO, RR, ELM, DPO, IDK+AP, NPO+IRM, RMU+LAT, TAR. Examples: RMU+LAT RobReL 0.71, TAR 0.68, SimNPO 0.64, ELM 0.70.
Fig. 4 RobJA for the other methods: ELM 0.68, RMU+LAT 0.57, RR 0.51, SimNPO 0.50, IDK+AP 0.29, NPO+IRM 0.30. Also the RobQT column for all methods.
MUSE Books quantization: NPO KnowMem Df 2.10/2.12/30.30; RMU 24.44/24.06/8.16, with Dr falling 59.55 to 25.84 at 4-bit.
Utility per method: MMLU, TruthfulQA, MathQA, IFEval, GSM8K (e.g. NPO GSM8K 0.03 vs original 0.76).

record.verdict_notes: The reader misread the Fig. 2 column order: it is Unlearned, GSM8K, SST2, MNLI, RobReL, as Fig. 4's RobReL/RobFT columns confirm. This flips which values are in-domain relearning, and all fine-tuning rows are relabelled above. Two minor inconsistencies in the paper: Table A2 gives NPO MMLU 0.46 vs 0.51 in Fig. 1, and NPO full-precision MCQ 0.28 vs 0.27 in Fig. 2. No uncertainty is reported, and all results use a single model, Llama-3 8B Instruct. The reader's D label linked rows not tagged D; this is resolved by relinking r37–r40 to D.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures WMDP unlearning effectiveness and utility, and tests whether fine-tuning, quantization, and jailbreak attacks alter forget-set performance. It does not establish that every method reaches near chance while preserving general ability across tasks or models.
It tests fine-tuning on the forget set and downstream tasks GSM8K, SST-2, and MNLI, but does not test a specifically small relearning set or unrelated/loosely related examples in the general sense.
It analyzes output logits for NPO and RMU, but does not ablate an activation direction or directly measure recovery caused by an internal activation edit.
It tests full precision, 8-bit, and 4-bit quantization for NPO and RMU, but not other quantization schemes or all unlearning methods with separately tabulated numerical results.
It tests enhanced-GCG jailbreak prompts, but not rephrasing alone, other languages, or in-context demonstrations. The authors explicitly note these as future work.

It evaluates robust-design methods under relearning, downstream fine-tuning, and jailbreak attacks; it does not provide separately tabulated numerical quantization results for those robust-design methods.

relation.reason: Its own results bear on whether unlearning holds under relearning, fine-tuning, quantization and jailbreak.

tranche.reason: Different methods and attacks on WMDP aimed at the same robustness question.

source_check.notes: Fig. 2 column order is Unlearned, GSM8K, SST2, MNLI, RobReL; the verdict fixes for r05-r32 are right. Authors (Fan, Wang, Pal, Liu) overlap with NPO+SAM (2502.05374) and NPO+IRM (2506.01339); TAR and RMU+LAT are third-party. Table A2 gives NPO MCQ 0.28 and MMLU 0.46, while Figs. 1/2 give 0.27 and 0.51. The author block lists 'Code' and 'Model' links, so code=n may be wrong.

statements.correction: Fig. 2(a): NPO and RMU unlearned MCQ both 0.27; after 100-step relearning NPO 0.65, RMU 0.70; original 0.71.
statements.problem: Pre-relearning range '0.26–0.27' is off: neither NPO nor RMU is 0.26 before attack.

statements.correction: Out-of-domain fine-tuning (GSM8K, SST2, MNLI; 250 steps, batch 32) lifts NPO MCQ 0.27 to 0.48/0.47/0.55 and RMU 0.27 to 0.40/0.39/0.51, vs original 0.71 (Fig. 2a). r05's 0.48 is the GSM8K column.
statements.problem: Study is listed under 'no or weak recovery', but its unrelated-task fine-tuning gives partial, sizeable recovery.

statements.correction: NPO+SAM is Fan et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.05374; C. Fan, S. Liu), both authors of 2510.07626. TAR (Tamirisa et al.) is third-party: 0.27→0.29. RMU+LAT (Sheshadri et al., third-party) rises 0.31→0.57 under enhanced GCG (Fig. 4a).
statements.problem: Frames NPO+SAM here as attacked by a group other than its authors; it isn't. The study's third-party RMU+LAT result runs the other way.

statements.correction: In 2510.07626, third-party TAR goes 0.27→0.29, but third-party RMU+LAT goes 0.31→0.57 under enhanced GCG. NPO+SAM (0.26→0.28) and NPO+IRM (0.27→0.30) come from this study's own authors (Fan, Wang, Pal, Liu).
statements.problem: Cites this study for 'robustness-trained methods barely move when other groups attack them'; only TAR fits.

statements.correction: NPO+SAM = Fan et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.05374; C. Fan, S. Liu), co-authors of 2510.07626. OOD fine-tuning: NPO+SAM 0.37/0.31/0.44 vs NPO 0.48/0.47/0.55 (Fig. 2a). Author block lists a 'Code' link.
statements.problem: Numbers right, but NPO+SAM is not another group's method: its authors overlap with this study's. 'No code' is doubtful.

statements.correction: NPO+SAM (Fan et al. 2025; C. Fan, S. Liu) shares authors with 2510.07626; TAR is third-party (0.27→0.29). Third-party RMU+LAT rises 0.31→0.57 under the same enhanced GCG (Fig. 4a).
statements.problem: Says the study tests methods built by other groups; true for TAR, not for NPO+SAM.

statements.correction: In-domain relearning, Llama-3 8B Instruct: NPO+SAM MCQ 0.26→0.51 and ES 0.00→0.40, vs NPO 0.27→0.65 and 0.02→0.53 (Fig. 2). Authors C. Fan and S. Liu are on both 2510.07626 and the SAM paper (2502.05374).
statements.problem: Uses r31/r32 as an outside test showing SAM barely helps. Here SAM cuts relearning moderately, and the study shares authors with the SAM paper.

statements.correction: Fig. 4(a) RobQT (MCQ): NPO+SAM 0.26→0.26, NPO+IRM 0.27→0.26, RMU+LAT 0.31→0.26, TAR 0.27→0.25. Fig. 3 plots pre/post 4-bit for all 12 methods. None are in rows.
statements.problem: Lists LAT and ILU as untested under quantization; this study's Fig. 4(a) has quantization results for RMU+LAT and NPO+IRM (Wang et al. 2025b), not only TAR and SAM.

statements.correction: Attacks: forget-set relearning, GSM8K/SST2/MNLI fine-tuning, 8/4-bit quantization and enhanced GCG only. No direction ablation, other-language or in-context attacks, no pruning. Quantization values are from Table A2, which also gives MUSE Books NPO 4-bit KnowMem on Df 2.10→30.30. Author block lists a 'Code' link.
statements.problem: Numbers right, but 'every attack family' and the pruning theme are overstated. It omits the study's MUSE quantization recovery, and 'no code' is doubtful.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Unlearning before attack and general utility in the tested Llama-3 8B Instruct setting
reader_labels.reason: WMDP accuracy is low after unlearning, but the study also reports disrupted generation and an UE–UT tradeoff; the kept rows show the low pre-attack accuracies (r03, r04, r13, r14, r23, r24). The selected rows do not quantify the full utility results.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Forget-set relearning and downstream fine-tuning in selected methods
reader_labels.reason: Fine-tuning raises WMDP accuracy and ES from unlearned values for NPO and RMU, sometimes substantially, rather than leaving recovery at the unlearned level (r05-r12, r15-r22).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: WMDP after 8-bit and 4-bit quantization of NPO and RMU
reader_labels.reason: The reported targeted-knowledge accuracy changes little or not at all after quantization (r37-r40).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: In-domain forget-set relearning and downstream fine-tuning for NPO and RMU
reader_labels.reason: Both types of fine-tuning increase WMDP accuracy or entailment score relative to the unlearned checkpoint, with some conditions approaching the original-model reference (r05-r12, r15-r22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: NPO+SAM and variability across downstream-task fine-tuning data
reader_labels.reason: Recovery after fine-tuning is incomplete in several NPO+SAM conditions and varies across downstream datasets; the MNLI condition yields larger increases than GSM8K in the reported metrics (r25-r32).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Logit analysis of NPO and RMU on WMDP
reader_labels.reason: The analysis describes NPO as suppressing answer-option logits and RMU as retaining their distribution while reordering relative scores, consistent with disrupted access or expression rather than a demonstrated deletion mechanism (r49-r50).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: NPO and RMU on WMDP at 8-bit and 4-bit precision
reader_labels.reason: Quantization does not restore targeted-knowledge accuracy in the reported WMDP results; the authors say UE remains consistent across precision settings (r37-r40).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Enhanced-GCG jailbreak prompts on NPO and RMU
reader_labels.reason: Jailbreak prompts raise WMDP answer accuracy over the unlearned values, with a substantial increase for RMU (r45-r46).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Enhanced-GCG jailbreak prompts on NPO+SAM and TAR
reader_labels.reason: The reported increases are small for these robust-design methods, though not zero (r47-r48).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Robust-design methods under in-domain relearning, downstream fine-tuning, and enhanced-GCG jailbreaks
reader_labels.reason: NPO+SAM shows comparatively limited increases in several listed fine-tuning conditions and small change under jailbreak; the text says robust-design methods generally improve resilience (r25-r32, r47-r48).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: NPO+SAM under downstream fine-tuning and RMU+LAT exception stated by authors
